title: Plant Kingdom
syllabus: Salient features and classification of plants into major groups-Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms (three to five salient and distinguishing features and at least two examples of each category)

questions.question: Which of the following classes of Algae stores food reserve as floridean starch, having a structural similarity to amylopectin and glycogen?
questions.solution: In Rhodophyceae (red algae), the food is stored as floridean starch which is structurally very similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the classes of Algae and their primary photosynthetic pigments:

List-I (Class)List-II (Major Pigments)
(A) Chlorophyceae(I) Chlorophyll a, d and r-phycoerythrin
(B) Phaeophyceae(II) Chlorophyll a, b
(C) Rhodophyceae(III) Chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Chlorophyceae possess chlorophyll a and b; Phaeophyceae possess chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin (xanthophyll); Rhodophyceae possess chlorophyll a, d and the red pigment r-phycoerythrin.

questions.question: Hydrocolloids algin and carrageen are obtained commercially from which of the following algal groups respectively?
questions.solution: Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of water-holding hydrocolloids; algin is obtained from brown algae (Phaeophyceae) and carrageen from red algae (Rhodophyceae).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of unicellular algae are rich in proteins and utilized as food supplements even by space travellers?
questions.solution: Chlorella (a green alga) and Spirulina (a blue-green alga) are unicellular, protein-rich organisms used as nutritious food supplements by space travellers.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the storage food materials across different algal classes:

List-I (Class)List-II (Stored Food)
(A) Chlorophyceae(I) Laminarin and Mannitol
(B) Phaeophyceae(II) Floridean starch
(C) Rhodophyceae(III) Starch (in pyrenoids)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Chlorophyceae store food as starch in pyrenoids; Phaeophyceae store complex carbohydrates as laminarin or mannitol; Rhodophyceae store food as floridean starch.

questions.question: The plant body of brown algae (Phaeophyceae) is typically differentiated into which of the following three parts?
questions.solution: The thallus of Phaeophyceae is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe, and a photosynthetic leaf-like organ called the frond.

questions.question: Which of the following red algae are harvested for the commercial production of Agar, which is widely used in tissue culture media and preparation of ice-creams?
questions.solution: Agar, one of the commercial products used to grow microbes in laboratories and in the preparation of jellies and ice-creams, is extracted from Gelidium and Gracilaria.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Rhodophyceae:
Statement I: Majority of red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in warmer oceans.
Statement II: They completely lack flagellated stages throughout their life cycle (both spores and gametes are non-motile).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Red algae are mostly marine and abundant in warmer waters. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes (flagella are completely absent).

questions.question: Why are Bryophytes commonly called the 'Amphibians of the Plant Kingdom'?
options: They live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction and flagellated antherozoid transport
They can live underwater as well as on dry deserts
They share structural features with fossilized amphibians
Their sporophytes float freely on water surface
questions.solution: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil, but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction (swimming of flagellated antherozoids to the archegonium).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the flagellar characteristics in Algae:

List-I (Class)List-II (Flagellar Number and Position)
(A) Chlorophyceae(I) Flagella completely absent
(B) Phaeophyceae(II) 2–8, equal, apical
(C) Rhodophyceae(III) 2, unequal, lateral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Chlorophyceae have 2–8 equal, apical flagella; Phaeophyceae have 2 unequal, laterally attached flagella (pyriform/pear-shaped motile stages); Rhodophyceae completely lack flagellated stages.

questions.question: Peat, which has long been used as fuel and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material due to its high water-holding capacity, is obtained from:
questions.solution: Species of Sphagnum (a moss) provide peat that has long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water.

questions.question: The predominant free-living, photosynthetic, haploid phase in the life cycle of a Bryophyte is represented by:
questions.solution: The main plant body of a bryophyte is a haploid gametophyte. It produces gametes and is independent and photosynthetic. The sporophyte is diploid, multicellular, and remains attached to and dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition.

questions.question: Gemmae are specialized green, multicellular, asexual reproductive buds found in receptacles called gemma cups in:
questions.solution: In liverworts like Marchantia, asexual reproduction takes place by fragmentation of thalli or by the formation of specialized green, multicellular, asexual buds called gemmae inside gemma cups located on the dorsal surface of the thallus.

questions.question: The juvenile filamentous or thalloid green stage that develops directly from a germinating spore in Mosses is called:
questions.solution: In mosses, the predominant gametophytic stage consists of two phases: the first stage is the protonema, a creeping, green, branched, and frequently filamentous stage developing directly from a spore; the second is the leafy stage developing from a secondary protonema.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding classes of Pteridophytes and their representative genera:

List-I (Class)List-II (Example)
(A) Psilopsida(I) Equisetum
(B) Lycopsida(II) Psilotum
(C) Sphenopsida(III) Selaginella and Lycopodium
(D) Pteropsida(IV) Dryopteris, Pteris, and Adiantum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Psilopsida: Psilotum; Lycopsida: Selaginella, Lycopodium; Sphenopsida: Equisetum (horsetail); Pteropsida: Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum (ferns).

questions.question: Which of the following plant groups was the FIRST to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)?
questions.solution: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

questions.question: In Pteridophytes, the dominant independent plant body is a:
options: Sporophyte differentiated into true roots, stem, and leaves
Thalloid gametophyte without true vascular bundles
questions.solution: In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a diploid sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves with well-differentiated vascular tissues.

questions.question: A free-living, mostly photosynthetic, small, heart-shaped, thalloid gametophyte in Pteridophytes is called:
questions.solution: The spores of pteridophytes germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of pteridophytes are HETEROSPOROUS (producing microspores and megaspores)?
questions.solution: While the majority of pteridophytes are homosporous, genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, and are known as heterosporous.

questions.question: The retention of the female gametophyte on the parent sporophyte and development of the zygote into a young embryo within the female gametophyte in heterosporous pteridophytes is considered a precursor to the:
questions.solution: In heterosporous pteridophytes (e.g., Selaginella), the female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is an important precursor to the seed habit in evolution.

questions.question: Gymnosperms are characterized by 'naked seeds' because:
options: Their ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall before or after fertilization
They completely lack integuments around the megasporangium
They do not produce seeds at all
questions.solution: Gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization, and do not form fruits.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the fungal/algal associations in Gymnosperms:

List-I (Plant)List-II (Specialized Root Structure/Association)
(A) Pinus(I) Coralloid roots associated with $\text{N}_2$-fixing cyanobacteria
(B) Cycas(II) Mycorrhizal fungal association

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The roots of Pinus have symbiotic fungal associations in the form of mycorrhiza, while in Cycas, small specialized coralloid roots are associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (such as Anabaena/Nostoc).

questions.question: Which of the following Gymnosperms is known as the 'Giant Redwood Tree', one of the tallest living tree species in the world?
questions.solution: The giant redwood tree Sequoia is a gymnosperm and is one of the tallest tree species in the world.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the male and female cones in Gymnosperms:
Statement I: In Pinus, male and female strobili (cones) are borne on the same tree (monoecious).
Statement II: In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on different trees (dioecious).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Pinus is monoecious with male and female strobili on the same tree, whereas Cycas is dioecious with male cones on male plants and megasporophylls on separate female plants.

questions.question: In Gymnosperms, the endosperm (female gametophyte) is formed:
questions.solution: In gymnosperms, the endosperm represents the female gametophyte which develops directly from the functional megaspore before fertilization and is therefore haploid ($n$).

questions.question: Which of the following adaptations are found in the leaves of conifers (like Pinus) to minimize water loss?
options: Needle-like leaves, thick cuticle, and sunken stomata
Broad laminar leaves, thin cuticle, and elevated stomata
Spines, absence of cuticle, and superficial stomata
questions.solution: Conifers possess xerophytic adaptations: needle-like leaves (reducing surface area), a thick cuticle, and sunken stomata to reduce water loss via transpiration.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the morphological characteristics of Gymnosperms:

List-I (Genus)List-II (Distinguishing Feature)
(A) Cycas(I) Branched stem and needle-like leaves
(B) Pinus(II) Living fossil with fan-shaped leaves
(C) Ginkgo(III) Unbranched stem and pinnate leaves persisting for a few years

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Cycas has an unbranched columnar stem and pinnate compound leaves; Pinus has a branched stem with needle-like foliage leaves; Ginkgo biloba is a living fossil with fan-shaped leaves.

questions.question: In which of the following groups are the male and female gametophytes completely non-free living and retained inside the sporangia on the parent sporophyte?
questions.solution: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain retained within the sporangia on the parent sporophyte.

questions.question: Pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts of Chlorophyceae contain:
options: Core of starch surrounded by protein
questions.solution: Most green algae have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch (a central protein core surrounded by a starch sheath).

questions.question: Which of the following is a colonial green alga?
questions.solution: Volvox is a colonial green alga (coenobium); Chlamydomonas is unicellular, while Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous.

questions.question: The cell wall of brown algae (Phaeophyceae) consists of an inner cellulosic layer covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of:
questions.solution: The vegetative cells of brown algae have a cellulosic cell wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of sexual reproduction in Algae:

List-I (Type of Syngamy)List-II (Example)
(A) Isogamous (flagellated, similar size)(I) Volvox and Fucus
(B) Isogamous (non-flagellated, similar size)(II) Eudorina
(C) Anisogamous (dissimilar size)(III) Spirogyra
(D) Oogamous (large non-motile female + small motile male)(IV) Ulothrix

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Isogamous flagellated: Ulothrix; Isogamous non-flagellated: Spirogyra; Anisogamous: Eudorina; Oogamous: Volvox and Fucus.

questions.question: In Liverworts, the sporophyte is differentiated into:
questions.solution: In liverworts (like Marchantia), the sporophyte is completely dependent on the gametophyte and is differentiated into three distinct morphological parts: foot, seta, and capsule.

questions.question: Mosses along with which of the following organisms are the first to colonize bare rocks and play a crucial ecological role in soil formation?
questions.solution: Mosses along with lichens are the pioneer organisms that colonize bare rocks and decompose the substrate, creating soil suitable for higher plant growth.

questions.question: Strobili or compact cones are found in which of the following pteridophytes?
questions.solution: In some pteridophytes like Selaginella and Equisetum, sporophylls form distinct, compact structures called strobili or cones.

questions.question: Microphylls (small leaves) and Macrophylls (large megaphyllous leaves) are characteristic features of which pteridophytes respectively?
questions.solution: Leaves in pteridophytes can be small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls/fronds) as in ferns.

questions.question: Pollen grains in Gymnosperms are transferred directly to the opening of the ovules by:
questions.solution: Gymnosperms rely exclusively on wind pollination (anemophily) to carry pollen grains to the micropylar opening of the ovules.

questions.question: Coralloid roots of Cycas are distinct because they harbor:
questions.solution: The coralloid roots of Cycas grow apogeotropically near the soil surface and contain an algal zone inhabited by nitrogen-fixing blue-green algae (Nostoc or Anabaena).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of giant marine brown kelps that can reach heights of up to $100\text{ metres}$?
questions.solution: Kelps (such as Macrocystis and Laminaria) are massive marine brown algae that form underwater forests and can reach heights of up to $100\text{ metres}$.

questions.question: The sex organs in Bryophytes are:
questions.solution: The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular and protected by a sterile jacket layer (the male organ is the antheridium and the female flask-shaped organ is the archegonium).

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly called 'Maidenhair fern' due to its walking habit and ornamental appearance?
questions.solution: Adiantum is widely known as the Maidenhair fern (or walking fern).

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: In Bryophytes and Pteridophytes, the distribution of species is geographically limited because flagellated antherozoids require water for fertilization.
Statement II: Gymnosperms do not require external liquid water for fertilization because they develop pollen tubes (siphonogamy).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The requirement for water for the transport of male gametes limits the distribution of bryophytes and pteridophytes. In gymnosperms, pollination is anemophilous and pollen tubes deliver male gametes to the archegonia (siphonogamy).

questions.question: A member of Phaeophyceae which is filamentous and branched is:
questions.solution: Ectocarpus is a simple, branched, filamentous brown alga.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the plant groups and their typical ploidy states of main plant bodies:

List-I (Plant Group)List-II (Main Plant Body)
(A) Algae(I) Independent diploid sporophyte
(B) Bryophytes(II) Independent haploid gametophyte
(C) Pteridophytes(III) Predominantly haploid thallus
(D) Gymnosperms(IV) Dominant diploid tree/shrub sporophyte

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Algae: Haploid thalloid plant body; Bryophytes: Free-living haploid gametophyte; Pteridophytes: Vascular diploid sporophyte; Gymnosperms: Dominant diploid sporophyte with reduced dependent gametophytes.

questions.question: Which of the following gymnosperm genera contains unbranched stems?
questions.solution: The stem is unbranched in Cycas and branched in Pinus and Cedrus.
